title: Hanuman Ansh Declared a Box Office Success After Miraculous Third-Week Surge
excerpt: The devotional drama collected approximately 8 crore rupees in 19 days after a massive word-of-mouth turnaround, with third-week earnings exceeding its first two weeks combined.
body:
• Hanuman Ansh collected ₹2.26-2.54 crore on Day 19, registering over 100% growth from the previous day on discounted ticket Tuesday.
  • The devotional drama’s 19-day total reached approximately ₹7.5-8 crore — a success for a film that opened to just ₹0.11 crore on Day 1.
  • Third-week collections already exceed the combined earnings of the first two weeks, marking one of the most dramatic box office turnarounds in recent memory.

Hanuman Ansh, the devotional drama that opened to near-invisible numbers three weeks ago, has been officially declared a box office success after a remarkable audience-driven resurgence carried its cumulative collections past ₹8 crore in 19 days.

The film collected approximately ₹2.26 crore nett on its third Tuesday (Day 19), according to Box Office India, registering over 100% growth from Monday’s ₹1.04 crore. The spike was amplified by discounted ticket prices on Tuesdays, a pattern that has consistently boosted the film’s midweek numbers. Bollywood Hungama pegged the Day 19 figure slightly higher at ₹2.54 crore.

A Turnaround for the Ages

The scale of Hanuman Ansh’s reversal is extraordinary by any measure. The film opened on August 7 to just ₹0.11 crore — a figure so low it barely registered on tracking platforms. Its first week yielded ₹1.07 crore, and Week 2 dropped further to ₹0.50 crore, suggesting the film would quietly exit theaters.

https://x.com/rameshlaus/status/2092529911085080987

Then word-of-mouth ignited. Weekend 3 exploded to ₹3.68 crore — a staggering 1,169% jump over Weekend 2’s ₹0.29 crore. Day 18 (Monday) brought ₹1.04 crore despite being a regular weekday, and Day 17 (Saturday) hit ₹1.84 crore. The third-week total through five days reached ₹6.75 crore nett, already exceeding the combined total of its first two weeks.

Projected Trajectory

Trade analysts project the third week will close around ₹9-10 crore nett, potentially pushing the lifetime total past ₹11 crore. For a film mounted on a limited budget, those numbers represent a clean hit.

“Such devotional films are unpredictable, as no one ever thought that this film could make a comeback after performing so poorly in the first weeks. That’s nothing but a miraculous turnaround, thanks to audience support and word-of-mouth,” Pinkvilla’s box office analysis noted.

The trajectory draws parallels to Laalo: Krishna Sada Sahaayate, which remained dormant for a month last year before audience discovery turned it into a theatrical hit — a reminder that devotional content operates on a different commercial logic than mainstream releases.

What’s Next

The immediate challenge is sustaining momentum against Toxic, the Yash-starrer that opened on August 26. Hanuman Ansh’s audience skews toward family and devotional viewers rather than the action-thriller demographic that Toxic targets, which could allow parallel runs without direct cannibalization.

As of Day 20, early estimates showed the film collecting approximately ₹1.43-1.51 crore, maintaining a strong hold. With 383 theaters still screening the film at roughly 50% occupancy, the theatrical run has significant room to extend.

Hanuman Ansh’s journey from a ₹0.11 crore opening to ₹9 crore in under three weeks stands as one of 2026’s most improbable box office stories — driven entirely by audiences rather than marketing spend.
